# Birth-death continuous {#sec-bd_continuous}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}

$$
    \frac{dN}{dt} = (b - d) N
$${#eq-birth-death-continuous}

This can be solved and the solution is  $N(t) = N_0 \, e^{(b-d)t} = N(0) e^{r t}$.

$r$ is growth rate and $N(0)$ is the initial population size at time = 0.

We can see here 

## Examples {.unnumbered}

Visualizing the function

Solving the equation
```{r}
library(deSolve)

# Parameters
b <- 0.5  # birth rate
d <- 0.1  # death rate
N0 <- 10  # initial population

# Birth-death model
bd_model <- function(time, state, params) {
  N <- state
  with(as.list(params),
    {
    dN <- (b - d) * N
    list(c(dN))}
  )
}

# Solve ODE
times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)
params1 <- c(b = 0.2, d = 0.1)
solution1 <- ode(y = N0, times = times, func = bd_model, parms = params1)

params2 <- c(b = 0.15, d = 0.1)
solution2 <- ode(y = N0, times = times, func = bd_model, parms = params2)

params3 <- c(b = 0.07, d = 0.1)
solution3 <- ode(y = N0, times = times, func = bd_model, parms = params3)

# Plot
plot(solution1, main = "Birth-Death Process", xlab = "Time", ylab = "Population")
lines(solution2, col = "red")
lines(solution3, col = "blue")
```

## Tips and warnings {.unnumbered}
```{r}
# Plot (b - d) * N as a function of N
b <- 0.2
d <- 0.1
N <- seq(0, 50, by = 1)
dN_dt <- (b - d) * N

plot(N, dN_dt, type = "l", main = "Birth-Death Rate", xlab = "Population (N)", ylab = "dN/dt")
grid()
```
